chapter: Clarence Williams's 1936 article and the dispute
title: Reading Clarence Williams's 1936 article: Buddy Bolden and Tiger Rag
summary: La Rocca has the 1936 Orchestra World article read, in which Williams says swing began in New Orleans with Bolden and that Tiger Rag was an old Black tune.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: And this is what I'd like you to read. It was in 1918. If I got 1819 down there, it's the wrong date. I wasn't even in. It would have to be 1918 that we had these Mama's Baby Boy and Brown Skin, who you fought? I want you to read this here, part of an article. He says, Swing, as they call it today, by Clarence Waino. From Honky Tonk to Swing.

All right. Let's see. This is from Orchestra World, 1936. Let's see. All right. Swing, as they call it today, was originated in New Orleans, the birthplace of Sister Kate and many other standard swing tunes, such as Tiger Rag. In those days, you could find in the slums of New Orleans such places as the Red Onion, the Keystone, Pete Lawless, and the Odd Fellows Hall, where the Eagle Band used to play. The Eagle Band was one of the highest bands in the country, with Buddy Bolden Cornetis, who had the world beat when it came to swing and jazz. Clarence stated that he heard him play when he, Clarence, was six or eight years old, and he was playing this same tune now called Tiger Rag, to which his mother and father used to dance the quadrille. That's spelled, quote, C-O-R-D-R-E-E-L, unquote. What he meant is quadrille.

It is an original Negro tune, which was made up down south. It was named Tiger Rag when the Dixieland Band brought it up north. Buddy, you want me to continue with this? Yeah, go on. Buddy Bolden was the hottest cornetist in the world, and he played so much that he is in the insane asylum now if he is still living. After this time came King Oliver, Punk, and Freddie Capron, that's spelled K-E-P-P-E-R-T, and the original Creole Band. They were the last word and swing cornet players. The swing pianists were Albert K-A-L, Cal, I suppose that's Carroll, Lewis Wade, Clarence Williams, Tony Jackson, Steve Lewis, and Jelly Roll Morton.
